definitions.explanation: The period spanning late December through early January, covering both the end of the old year and the beginning of the new year. A major holiday season in Japan when most businesses close.

examples.japanese: {年末年始|ねんまつねんし}は{実家|じっか}で{過|す}ごす。
examples.english: I spend the year-end and New Year period at my parents' house.

examples.japanese: {年末年始|ねんまつねんし}の{休|やす}みは12{月|がつ}29{日|にち}から1{月|がつ}3{日|か}までです。
examples.english: The year-end and New Year holiday is from December 29 to January 3.

examples.japanese: {年末年始|ねんまつねんし}は{帰省|きせい}ラッシュで{新幹線|しんかんせん}も{高速道路|こうそくどうろ}も{混雑|こんざつ}する。
examples.english: During the year-end and New Year period, the bullet trains and expressways are crowded due to the rush of people returning home.

notes:
USAGE:
A compound of {年末|ねんまつ} (year-end) and {年始|ねんし} (beginning of the year). The typical {年末年始|ねんまつねんし} holiday for companies and government offices runs from December 29 to January 3. This is one of the three major holiday periods in Japan, along with Golden Week and Obon. Major activities include {大掃除|おおそうじ} (year-end cleaning), {年賀状|ねんがじょう} (New Year's cards), and {初詣|はつもうで} (first shrine visit).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {年末年始|ねんまつねんし}の{休|やす}み: year-end/New Year holiday
- {年末年始|ねんまつねんし}{休業|きゅうぎょう}: closed for year-end/New Year
- {年末年始|ねんまつねんし}を{過|す}ごす: to spend the year-end/New Year period
- {年末年始|ねんまつねんし}の{営業|えいぎょう}: year-end/New Year business hours
